ev.q: Findings from BRFSS indicate that approximately 7.2% of U.S. adults have current asthma.
The overall prevalence of lifetime asthma among adults was 11.0% (95% CI = 10.8%--11.2%)
Among respondents with current asthma, 82.7% reported no visits to an ED during the preceding 12 months
The overall prevalence of lifetime asthma among adults was 11.0% (95% CI = 10.8%--11.2%)
Among the 50 states, current asthma prevalence ranged from 5.3% (Louisiana and South Dakota) to 9.5% (Massachusetts).
South Dakota was above the CI on six of seven questions, indicating above-average asthma control.
BRFSS is a state-based, random-digit--dialed survey of the noninstitutionalized civilian U.S. population
The 2001 BRFSS lifetime prevalence estimate (11.0%) was slightly higher than the 2000 BRFSS lifetime estimate (10.5%).
This report summarizes asthma prevalence data for adults collected from the 2001 BRFSS survey

methods_quotes.q: Weighted prevalence estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated by using SUDAAN to account for the complex survey design
Current asthma was defined as answering "yes" to the lifetime question and to the question
